text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Special Duties Minister Wole Oyelese alleges that opposition groups are planning to disrupt local council polls scheduled for next month.
- Three soldiers killed in clash between men of Edo state forestry task force and log carriers.
- Demand for foreign exchange at weekly auction rises to $90.36 million this week from $76.88 last week.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha and other Nigerian leaders urge Nigerians to embrace peace and tolerance as Moslems in the country mark end of Ramadan fast.
- Five editors of the Tribune newspapers published in Ibadan in the southwest are sacked in major reorganisation of the independent publications.
- Nigeria lost an estimated one billion naira last year by not exporting all the cashew nuts in its warehouses because of poor quality, says leader of newly formed cashew association.
- Nigerian inflation projected to have dropped to 26.8 percent in January from 28 percent in December.
- Police gear up to investigate cases of contractors who did not execute their jobs and who will be charged before failed contracts tribunals to be set up soon, police sources say.
- Electoral commission releases materials for registration of voters which commences nationwide on Monday.

- A floating storage vessel for the $569 million Escravos Gas project of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation and Chevron Corp joint venture has set sail to Nigeria for the project commissioning scheduled for May.
